ops.title: hermes-agent-setup activation aborts on externalized stateDir (chown EPERM on virtiofs mountpoint)
ops.description: Found 2026-07-07 during the first live 'just redeploy hermes': upstream nixosModules.nix:732 does an unguarded 'chown/chmod' of cfg.stateDir; /var/lib/hermes is a virtiofs mountpoint that EPERMs both, and activation snippets run set -e, so the setup TAIL (subdir perms, config.yaml merge, env assembly) is SKIPPED and switch exits rc=1 every time. Ownership is already correct (hermes:hermes 755) — only the mountpoint syscalls fail. Routes explored: no upstream skip-option exists; module comes from hermes-agent.nixosModules.default (flake-parts wrapped, so no disabledModules/patched-import path); patchedHermesSrc only feeds the package, not the module. RECOMMENDED: upstream PR guarding the stateDir chown/chmod with 'mountpoint -q' (benefits every externalized-state user; add to the existing watch task flow), with a local lib.mkForce override of system.activationScripts.hermes-agent-setup (copy of upstream text + guard + a hash-drift assert against the module input) as the stopgap if a redeploy must go green sooner.

ops.text: just redeploy hermes exits 0 and journal shows hermes-agent-setup completing (config.yaml merge line) on an externalized stateDir
